comparator.name: Rechtsgeleerdheid (Dutch Law)
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 regulations describe a three-year, 180 EC Dutch Law degree. Students build on introductory law courses to enter later semesters. Legal and professional skills run alongside the law courses. The final year includes 12 EC of electives and an 18 EC thesis sequence, with 3 EC of research methods and 15 EC for the individual thesis. The public curriculum page also previews a separate 2027–2028 plan.

Constitutional and administrative law, with administrative procedure, tax law and employment law as related public-law fields: the principles of the Dutch state, the powers of government and the legal protection of citizens, taught in an introduction in year 1 and the integrated course Staats- en Bestuursrecht in year 2

Foundations of law: the introductory and year-3 courses Grondslagen van het Recht, which the final qualifications describe as historical, philosophical, legal-theoretical and psychological perspectives on law

Legal reasoning, argumentation and legal skills: logic and interpretation methods, building and defending a legal argument, changing position and presenting the counter-argument, written and oral communication, taught through the Juridische Vaardigheden courses and problem-based small-group education, with simulated court proceedings

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The plans share seven law courses and five other courses. Law and Society develops qualitative research and social theory and uses them to investigate environmental justice, technology governance, media and race, gender and youth extremism. The closest plan develops commercial law, political institutions and argumentation. Each plan has twelve courses, or 90 EC, unique to it.

The entrepreneurship gateway precedes Transnational Business Law, and Research Methods & Statistics precedes Public Economics. Introductory rhetoric precedes persuasion and community debate. alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest plan covers the broad legal core with comparative law, private and commercial law, legal reasoning and related skills. Law and Society develops the programme interests in everyday law, legal responses to social problems and applying principles to current issues. Each plan has 90 EC of courses that the other lacks. A separate criminal-law direction could use criminal accountability and organised crime, with social context from youth resilience and media coverage of crime. UCR has limited depth in criminal procedure and no dedicated follow-on criminal-law course. A separate international and European law direction could draw on trade governance, European politics, conflict and international relations. The closest plan already covers the three main overlapping law courses and the institutional context. The additional courses develop international politics or trade, with limited additional legal depth. The two options therefore retain the relevant criminal and international courses within their broader curricula.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce legal traditions and ways of thinking about law. UCR also examines law as a social institution.
Both draw on history and philosophy. UCR focuses on the foundations of human rights. Maastricht also covers legal theory and the psychology of law.
Both introduce private law. UCR uses comparative examples in property, tort and contract. Maastricht introduces the Dutch system of private rights and obligations.
Both study contracts and remedies. UCR focuses on cross-border commercial transactions and arbitration. Maastricht studies Dutch obligations more broadly, including tort and unjust enrichment.
Maastricht studies jurisdiction and choice of law in cross-border private disputes. UCR covers related commercial disputes within Transnational Business Law.
UCR studies property within Principles of Private Law. Maastricht provides a separate course.
Maastricht provides dedicated study of Dutch company and insolvency law.
Maastricht provides a dedicated course on property between partners and succession.
Maastricht provides a dedicated Dutch employment law course. UCR addresses employment in the context of transnational business.
Maastricht provides a dedicated course on Dutch civil procedure.
Both study limits on government power, rights and judicial review. UCR compares legal systems and covers administrative law within that comparison.
UCR covers public authority and administrative remedies within comparative constitutional law.
UCR covers this area within Comparative Constitutional Law, paired below with Maastricht’s combined constitutional and administrative law course.
Maastricht provides a separate course on administrative procedure. UCR covers administrative remedies and procedural fairness within Comparative Constitutional Law.
Public Economics covers taxation and redistribution. Maastricht studies tax law.
Both study criminal liability and the principles of criminal law. Maastricht also introduces criminal procedure.
Maastricht extends the study of criminal law and criminal procedure in Year 3. UCR covers core criminal law in a single course.
Both introduce the sources and subjects of international law. Maastricht also introduces EU law in this course.
UCR examines EU institutions, competences, legal sources and enforcement. Maastricht combines EU law with further study of public international law.
Both develop first-year academic and professional skills. Maastricht includes coaching and portfolio work across a three-year sequence.
Maastricht trains students to read legal sources and reason through Dutch legal problems. UCR develops related argument skills across several courses.
Maastricht continues training in legal argument and interpretation of Dutch legal sources.
Maastricht has a further module in practical legal skills.
Maastricht continues its coached professional skills sequence in Year 2.
Maastricht completes its professional skills sequence in Year 3.
Students can use the final 12 EC for an internship, faculty or external courses, or an approved project or research option.
Maastricht requires a research proposal and an individual thesis. UCR methods courses develop empirical research skills, and optional independent research sits outside the scheduled courses.
